page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-8x.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz, paired with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by eight NVIDIA A10 GPUs offering a cumulative total of 192 GB of GDDR6 VRAM, with 24 GB allocated per GPU. Networking capability is backed by a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating heavy communication throughput across distributed workloads. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent operating system and data storage needs, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high concentration of eight GPUs within a single system provides dense graphics and inference throughput relative to footprint overhead. This setup minimizes multi-node communication penalties for models that fit within 192 GB of aggregate VRAM. Workloads suited for this hardware configuration include distributed deep learning inference, graphics virtualization, video processing pipelines, and AI-driven computer vision tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-8x.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for high-density computing workloads. Based on the x86_64 architecture and virtualized via KVM, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz alongside 256 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. The instance integrates eight NVIDIA A10 GPUs offering 192 GB of combined VRAM, suited for parallelized graphical and machine learning computations. Network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dense ratio of eight GPUs to 64 vCPUs makes it suitable for concurrent AI inference, multi-stream video encoding, rendering, and computer vision pipelines.
